## RatifierUtils namespace

Utilities for selecting Midnight ratifier routes.

Call these during make-side preparation, before `Offer.create`<!-- -->, when an app must decide whether a maker can sign an Ecrecover root or must approve a Setter root onchain. Fetch helpers read bytecode for you; this namespace is the pure classification logic.

**Signature:**

```typescript
export declare namespace RatifierUtils
```

## Example


```ts
import { RatifierUtils } from "@morpho-org/midnight-sdk";

console.log(RatifierUtils.isEip7702Designator("0xef0100"));
```

[getRatifierInfo(params)](./midnight-sdk.ratifierutils.getratifierinfo.md)


</td><td>

Selects Ecrecover for EOAs/EIP-7702 accounts and Setter for deployed-code accounts.

Use the returned `ratifier` address in `Offer.create`<!-- -->. Later, use `EcrecoverRatifierUtils.ratify` when `type` is `ecrecover`<!-- -->, or approve the root and call `SetterRatifierUtils.ratify` when `type` is `setter`<!-- -->.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[isEip7702Designator(bytecode)](./midnight-sdk.ratifierutils.iseip7702designator.md)


</td><td>

Checks whether bytecode is an EIP-7702 designator.

EIP-7702 accounts have code-like bytecode but still sign as the owning EOA, so they use the Ecrecover ratifier route instead of the Setter route.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[normalizeRatifierTree(params)](./midnight-sdk.ratifierutils.normalizeratifiertree.md)


</td><td>

Normalizes a ratifier tree input and asserts it uses one ratifier address.

Pass an existing `Tree` or `TreeLike` object to reuse cached offers, leaves, root, and height. Pass raw offer/group input when the caller has not materialized a tree yet.


</td></tr>
